title: RegionSeal: Atomic FPGA Artifacts at the Unchanged GGML Boundary
hook: Against the current strict backend's 11 accepted operator families and 112 graph signatures, RegionSeal adds exactly one recurring-region artifact and no new operator-family wrapper, yet predicts a measurable pp512 or tg128 wall-clock reduction while retaining the same GGML admission and failure boundary.
hook_shape_rationale: This is counter-intuitive minimalism: the strongest local baseline's breadth axis is its 11-family, 112-signature strict FPGA path, while the candidate is no broader on operator support and adds only one independently replaceable artifact. A surprising empirical reveal was also viable, but rejected because the direction of launch/wait reduction is expected; the defensible surprise is that one narrowly sealed region can test useful acceleration without whole-graph ownership or all-family vectorization.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf establishes that a framework-native backend can retain exact support decisions, explicit failure behavior, tensor-state continuity, and accelerator-artifact identity while execution no longer incurs one host-visible completion cycle per admitted unit — stakes: backend maintainers otherwise face either silent semantic drift and wrong outputs or a formally correct integration whose launch overhead blocks useful deployment and wastes FPGA development effort.
gap_closure.how_closed: C13 encodes the GGML tensor-effect connectivity as a verifiable region seal, and heterogeneous_decomposition uses that seal to substitute one pure effect-closed recurring region while mutable or externally aliased work stays on the strict per-node FPGA path; corpus support is thin in FPGA runtimes, with the closest C13 exemplars coming from relational-topology domains.

core_mechanism: RegionSeal first assigns every backend allocation a monotonic allocation_id and represents a tensor T by F(T) = {(allocation_id, [o + sum_k i_k nb_k, o + sum_k i_k nb_k + s_k)) for every valid logical index tuple i}, where o is the tensor's root-view byte offset, nb_k are GGML byte strides, and s_k is the stored byte width for the F16 element at that index; interval unions are normalized, bounds-checked, and derived from the complete GGML tensor metadata before launch. For every already-accepted node, a read/write effect is the pair of normalized footprint sets it may read and write, obtained from the operator implementation's explicit operand-role table rather than inferred from names. A candidate region is effect-closed only if every node is pure, every internal read is supplied by a region input or earlier region write, no write intersects any immutable input or tensor outside the region, every terminal output has no external storage-range alias, and the region contains no KV update, in-place mutation, or externally visible state. Among repeated contiguous DAG regions of length 2 through 6 in the complete pp512 and tg128 traces, the sole implemented region R* is selected by maximum baseline XRT wait time attributable to its occurrences, with ties broken by more occurrences and then lexicographic serialized GGML signature; thus no free region choice is left to the implementer. structural_prior_encoding produces the region seal: a digest over ordered node signatures, canonical effects, boundary tensor types/shapes/strides, the artifact kernel UUID, bounded loop limits, and a status schema, and a static checker certifies the stated disjointness and effect-closure conditions under the captured graph and allocation metadata. heterogeneous_decomposition consumes that seal by routing only exact R* matches to one finite HLS artifact and leaving every other accepted node, including all mutable or aliased state, on the existing strict per-node FPGA path rather than CPU fallback. The artifact executes synchronously into fresh output BOs, writes one status record, and has no externally outstanding dependent kernel; after one xrt::run wait, the backend publishes the fresh BO bindings only when both XRT and artifact status report success, otherwise it discards them and returns the existing explicit backend error with prior tensor bindings unchanged. Because publication changes only unaliased terminal tensor bindings and retains their GGML objects, types, dimensions, strides, and ownership records, later strict nodes observe continuous tensor state while a fault cannot strand a dependency or expose a partial candidate output. The novelty claim is the independently replaceable, digest-bound region contract and atomic publication rule at the unchanged GGML backend boundary, not the ordinary fact that R*'s arithmetic is combined inside one artifact.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES ledger:
P1. GGML views and backend tensors expose sufficient root allocation, offset, shape, stride, and type metadata to derive exact F16 byte footprints; the current backend already resolves these fields to launch accepted operators.
P2. Pure recurring regions exist in both llama-bench pp512 and tg128 traces — untested — falsification target; recurrence and attributable wait mass must be established from the supplied complete traces before R* is built.
P3. A strict node outside R* can consume a successfully rebound backend BO without changing its support decision; this follows from support being keyed by operator/type/shape and is verified against all downstream R* consumers.
P4. A finite single artifact plus one synchronous wait has no unresolved cross-kernel dependency after return; all loop bounds are sealed and any XRT timeout or nonzero status is propagated before publication.
observation-model: the 2,422 accepted U280 dispatch observations and pp512/tg128 traces are complete for the measured Gemma 3 1B F16 llama-bench runs because hooks record every accepted GGML call, XRT start, and wait, but they are not an unbiased sample of other models or prompts, so claims remain scoped to this path.
ESTIMAND: for each fixed llama-bench regime pp512 and tg128 on the baseline Gemma 3 1B F16 GGUF and one U280, the target is the paired median end-to-end wall-clock time across 30 post-warmup runs, together with the fraction of baseline XRT wait time and starts attributable to exact R* occurrences.
BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT: The naive runnable version detects a repeated GGML node sequence, replaces it with one fused XRT kernel, and writes directly to the original destination BO. Branch (i): it falsely assumes node sequence, shape, and tensor name determine non-aliasing and that a failed launch may safely have touched the destination; legal GGML views can overlap one canonical allocation, so RegionSeal confronts this with exact allocation-range effects, exclusion of external aliases, fresh output BOs, and publish-after-success. Alias/effect analysis is a standard compiler tool, but this instance is not solved by that tool alone because an unchanged GGML backend neither owns graph rewriting nor may change per-node admission, explicit no-fallback behavior, XRT artifact identity, or tensor-storage lifetime; the seal binds those runtime-specific obligations to an independently replaceable artifact.
BLOCK 3 — The anchor is one gap with a chain, so the same seal is deliberately the intermediate object: structural encoding constructs it and heterogeneous decomposition consumes it; no auxiliary module is added. Ordinary fusion, command capture, a persistent overlay, compiler-owned dataflow, asynchronous version polling, and MVCC/COW epochs were rejected because they land on occupied lineage nodes or recreate progress and alias hazards; direct writes were rejected because failure could expose partial storage, and all-11 wrappers were rejected because one R* is sufficient for the minimal wall-clock test.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Add allocation_id and root-view tracking to the existing GGML FPGA tensor metadata; input GGML tensor descriptors produce normalized, overflow-checked F16 footprint interval sets keyed by the owning XRT BO.
2. Add explicit read/write operand-role tables for the currently accepted implementations and run the effect extractor before graph launch; input nodes and canonical footprints produce per-node effects plus overlap edges.
3. Scan the existing complete Gemma 3 1B F16 pp512/tg128 traces for repeated contiguous DAG regions of two to six pure accepted nodes, reject any region with KV mutation, in-place writes, external aliases, or non-closed effects, and deterministically emit R* using the wait-mass selection rule.
4. Serialize R* into a region-seal manifest containing node signatures, boundary metadata, normalized effects, bounded dimensions, status codes, and artifact UUID; the manifest checker either emits a digest-qualified substitution entry or leaves every node on the current strict FPGA path.
5. Implement and synthesize exactly one U280 HLS artifact for R*, reusing the current arithmetic kernels where practical but writing terminal results to fresh BOs and a status record; its output is one xclbin kernel whose bounded control returns only after all R* arithmetic completes.
6. At the unchanged GGML graph-compute boundary, rerun the seal check against live allocation_ids and ranges, start the digest-matched artifact once, and synchronously wait once; a mismatch executes the same accepted nodes through the current strict per-node FPGA path, never CPU fallback.
7. On successful XRT wait and zero artifact status, atomically replace each unaliased terminal tensor's backend BO ownership record with its fresh BO so downstream GGML nodes consume the new values; on timeout or fault, retain old bindings, release staging BOs after device reset/quiescence, and return the existing explicit error.
8. Add regression tests with overlapping offset/strided views, allocation reuse, forced digest mismatch, injected nonzero artifact status, XRT timeout, and downstream consumers; outputs are compared with the unchanged CPU path and current strict FPGA path, and every negative case must preserve old bindings and produce no fallback.
9. Run llama-bench pp512 and tg128 on the existing Gemma 3 1B F16 GGUF for 30 post-warmup repetitions per arm, recording end-to-end wall clock, GGML calls, XRT starts/waits, outputs, tokens, status traces, allocation publications, and artifact UUIDs for strict baseline, RegionSeal, and manifest-disabled control.
falsification_prediction: On one Alveo U280, run the unchanged llama.cpp llama-bench executable and the existing Gemma 3 1B F16 GGUF in pp512 and tg128 modes for 30 post-warmup repetitions under the current strict backend and RegionSeal, then compare paired median end-to-end wall clock, XRT starts/waits, output tensors, and generated tokens. If the candidate works, at least one of pp512 or tg128 has lower median full-path wall clock, exact R* occurrences collapse to one start and one wait each, CPU fallback remains zero, and outputs satisfy the current matched-reference checks. The load-bearing variable is sealed wait coverage W_R, defined as baseline XRT wait time attributable to exact effect-closed R* occurrences divided by baseline end-to-end time; the negative control forces W_R to zero by disabling only the seal digest match while retaining all instrumentation and is predicted to move end-to-end wall clock back toward the strict baseline. Fault injection and overlapping-view tests are a second falsifier: any published BO after nonzero status, any changed aliased byte, any missing explicit error, or no wall-clock movement despite substantial W_R falsifies the contract or performance mechanism.
compute_budget: 0 GPU-day + $0 API; approximately 14-18 engineer-weeks, one U280, 40-80 Vitis synthesis/place-and-route runs, and about 200 board-hours, feasible within five months.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Its selector replays measured per-operator and directed transition costs without an integrated runtime, whereas RegionSeal constructs and executes a live digest-bound GGML region with canonical BO-range effects, one synchronous completion, and publish-after-success storage semantics.

Its host agent may choose CPU execution and retrieves FPGA output before subsequent layer progress, whereas RegionSeal preserves zero fallback and substitutes only a statically effect-closed pure region while every excluded node remains on the existing strict FPGA path.

ATLAS generates whole-model hardware through a universal GEMM abstraction, whereas RegionSeal constructs a single independently replaceable artifact contract over native GGML signatures, canonical view ranges, failure status, and atomic BO publication at the unchanged backend boundary (abstract-only inference because its full text is unavailable in the supplied cache).

what_step_was_missed: ATLAS would have needed to derive canonical GGML allocation-range effects and bind them, explicit failure status, artifact identity, and publish-after-success tensor rebinding into a per-region contract that remains valid without owning or rewriting the application graph.
